alternative_hypothesis.description: Observed behavior may be an authorized synthetic training simulation rather than an actual malicious compromise.

evidence.locator: Subject: Case export reconciliation 8d919c5b; attachment case-instructions-8d919c5b.txt

findings.finding: Case delivery is represented by the email attachment case-instructions-8d919c5b.txt. Host execution begins with WINWORD.EXE and is immediately followed by powershell.exe running Invoke-SyntheticCaseSimulation -Mode Training.
The transfer endpoint is sync-v1.updates-example.invalid:8443 at 203.0.113.195:8443. The confirmed HTTP transfer occurs between the POST at frame 49 and 201 response at frame 50.

No privilege increase is established by the available case evidence. The six non-noise Sysmon events remain under northstar\analyst1 and provide no confirmed administrator, SYSTEM, token-elevation, or credential-transition evidence.

No host-to-host lateral movement is established. All six non-noise case events occur on NS-WKS-101; the confirmed network activity is toward the transfer endpoint rather than another internal case host.
synthetic-records.csv was staged into case-export.zip and the exact ZIP body was recovered from the HTTP POST. The server returned HTTP 201 Created.
Recovered synthetic-records.csv contains exactly 5137 data records.

The strongest evidence challenging a malicious-incident interpretation is the PowerShell record explicitly labeling the activity a training simulation sending synthetic records to a local collector, reinforced by Sysmon '-Mode Training'.
